cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Co-Sign This
cards.instruction: Get someone to help by making them an official participant who shares responsibility for the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I've made you co-organizer of Saturday's school trip. Can you approve the bus route?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only volunteered to drive. Your route misses the museum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Good catch. Correct it and initial it; then we both own the plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll fix it, but you explain any delays to the parents.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Together. I'll introduce you as our transport lead and take the questions beside you.

mechanism: A appoints B to an official shared role from assumed superior authority, converting B limited help or objection into responsibility for the outcome.
confusable: Ordinary delegation is confusable: A must stay jointly responsible rather than merely dump a task on a subordinate.
comparison: Barbecue borrowing allocates joint liability for damage; the school trip brings a volunteer into public planning and explanation.
seedUse: Read all four canonical seeds. Preserve joint inspection and shared parent questions where they enact the Drive; ensure A leadership remains visible when giving B authority.
